October 24, 2026

Executives quit $25bn Alaska gas venture over alleged hidden Russian control

tags: politics, markets
sources: @aaronparnas

A Financial Times investigation reported that US executives resigned from a $25 billion Alaska gas venture over claims that the project was secretly under Russian control. Separate New York Times reporting said a sanctioned Russian energy company covertly financed an American firm pitching the Alaska project, with the involvement concealed through a UAE-linked intermediary. The project was said to have been discussed in Ukraine peace talks, with Vladimir Putin raising the idea with envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, though there is no indication either knew of the Russian ties. The White House was reportedly warned about the Russian financing and urged to investigate.

White House aides brace for Trump firings if Republicans lose Congress

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

With ten days until election day, White House officials are reportedly anticipating an all-out push by President Trump to fire staff and reassign personnel if Republicans lose at least one chamber of Congress. According to CNN and other outlets, significant internal jockeying has begun as aides conclude the president is becoming a lame duck. Democrats retaking the House of Representatives would stall the administration's legislative agenda, which has produced limited results to date.

Trump weighing mass pre-emptive pardons for junior White House staff

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

President Trump is considering mass pardons for junior staffers in the White House and the wider executive branch, according to reporting from the Washington Sun. Accepting a pardon removes Fifth Amendment protection against self-incrimination for the pardoned offences, meaning recipients could no longer decline to testify about them. Pre-emptive pardons on that scale would also signal a belief that the staffers may have been involved in criminal conduct.

Musk spends over $470m on midterms amid fears of congressional investigations

tags: politics, tech
sources: @aaronparnas

Elon Musk is reported to be deeply concerned about the prospect of Republicans losing the midterm elections, which would expose him to congressional investigations and subpoenas. Democrats have placed him near the top of their list for scrutiny, covering SpaceX, Starlink, USAID contracts and the Department of Government Efficiency. He has spent more than $470 million on the current election cycle, more than in any previous campaign.

Trump remarks in Florida renew questions about his cognitive state

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

President Trump delivered disjointed remarks at an appearance in Florida, moving from a claim about US military equipment and Venezuela to an unfinished reference to "the national" before switching to the Islamic Republic of Iran. At one point he appeared to instruct himself aloud to "think of it" mid-sentence. The episode follows other recent incidents that have drawn attention to his delivery and apparent lapses.

Fox News campus interview turns to complaints about prices and the economy

tags: politics, media, economy
sources: @aaronparnas

A Fox News reporter interviewing college students at a Trump rally asked what they hoped to hear from the president and which issues mattered to them this election cycle. A student said he wanted relief from the war, lower inflation and lower interest rates, describing current prices for shopping and fuel as absurd. The reporter moved the microphone away and ended the exchange.
